title: רב דימי אחוה דרב ספרא

paragraphs: Rav Dimi, brother of Rav Safra. He died without leaving instructions, and they came before Rava—a scribal error; it should read before Rabbi Abba. He said, “I know Rav Dimi was not wealthy,” and returned the deposit in his possession to that man: Ketubbot 85b. In Arakhin 16 he fell ill, and his brother Rav Safra came in to inquire after him. He said, “May it be credited to me that I fulfilled everything the sages said.” He answered, “Did you fulfill, ‘One should never speak of his fellow’s good qualities’?” He replied, “I did not know; had I known, I would have fulfilled it.” In Bava Batra 164b, Rav Dimi, brother of Rav Safra, teaches: “One should never speak of his fellow’s good qualities, for through his praise ….” So too in the aforementioned Arakhin, except that it says, “Some say: he fell ill and said, ‘May it be credited …’; he answered, ‘Did you fulfill …?’” Semag, negative commandment 9, brings this Gemara and explains “One should not speak …” as in the presence of his enemy. See Yehudah Chayyati, what is written there.
